title: 12 Animal Facts That Sound FAKE But Are 100% Real (TRUE or FALSE?)
blurb: TRUE or FALSE? Cube-shaped poop, three hearts, a mammal that glows... most of these sound made up, and most are real. Three are fakes. Guess before the 3-second timer, keep score, and drop your score out of 12 in the comments 👇
next: Subscribe: tomorrow it's the myths about the animals in your own house.
pinned:
📝 SCORE CHECK: how many did you get out of 12? 👇

Answer key: FALSE = flamingos born pink, ostrich fastest, duck quack doesn't echo. Everything else is REAL.

Which one do you STILL not believe?

beats.say: Cube shaped poop. Three hearts. An animal that glows in the dark. Some of these facts sound completely made up, and most of them are real. Your job is to catch the fakes.
You get three seconds to guess true or false. Keep score, and tell me your number out of twelve at the end. Three of these are lies. Let's go.
True or false? Wombats poop cubes.
beats.bonus: Wombats leave their cubes on rocks and logs to mark their territory, and the flat sides stop them rolling away.

beats.say: True! Square poop. From a round animal.

A wombat can leave dozens of little cubes in a single night. Scientists worked out that the end of its intestine has stiff and stretchy sections, and as the poop moves through, it gets pressed into corners.
And wombats are tougher than they look. Their backside is mostly a hard plate of cartilage, so when a predator follows them into a burrow, the wombat just blocks the tunnel with its rear end.
The cubes are useful too. Wombats stack them on rocks and logs to mark their territory, and because they're flat sided, they don't roll away.
The researchers who figured it out won an Ig Nobel Prize. That's a real award for research that makes you laugh, then think.
beats.text:
A REAL PRIZE
FOR POOP
RESEARCH

beats.say: True or false? Octopuses have three hearts.
beats.bonus: An octopus has blue blood, because it uses copper instead of iron to carry oxygen.

beats.say: True. And that's not even the weirdest part.
Two small hearts pump blood through the gills, and one big heart pumps it around the rest of the body.
Here's the wild bit. When an octopus swims, the main heart actually stops beating for a moment. That's one reason octopuses would rather crawl than swim. Swimming is exhausting.
And their blood is blue. Three hearts, blue blood, and eight arms. Basically an alien that lives in the sea.
True or false? Sea otters hold hands while they sleep.
beats.quiz:
SEA OTTERS HOLD
HANDS WHILE
THEY SLEEP
beats.bonus: Sea otters have the thickest fur of any animal, up to about a million hairs in a single square inch.

beats.say: True. And it's not just for cuteness.
Sea otters sleep floating on their backs, so holding paws, or wrapping themselves in seaweed, keeps them from drifting apart while they nap.

Sea otters are also one of the few animals that use tools. They float on their backs, put a rock on their belly, and smash shellfish open on it. Some even keep a favorite rock tucked in a pocket of skin under their arm.
A group of resting otters is called a raft. Sometimes there are dozens of them, all bobbing together like a furry pool party.
So yes, they hold hands. Science says it's practical. Everyone else says it's adorable. Both are right.
True or false? Flamingos are born pink.
beats.bonus: A flamingo can sleep standing on one leg, and scientists think it may take less effort than standing on two.

beats.say: False. Baby flamingos are grey and white. Fluffy little grey potatoes.
They turn pink from what they eat. Algae and tiny shrimp are full of natural colors called carotenoids, and those end up in their feathers.
A flamingo that eats less of that food slowly fades to pale pink or white. So a bright pink flamingo is basically a well fed flamingo.
You are what you eat. For flamingos, that's literally true.
beats.text:
YOU ARE WHAT
YOU EAT.
LITERALLY.

beats.say: True or false? A starfish can regrow a lost arm.
beats.quiz:
A STARFISH CAN
REGROW AN ARM
beats.bonus: Starfish have no blood. They pump sea water around their bodies instead.

beats.say: True. And some can do something even crazier.
If a starfish loses an arm, it can slowly grow a new one. And in some species, a single arm with a piece of the center attached can grow into a whole new starfish.
Starfish also have a tiny eye spot at the tip of each arm. They can't see detail, but they can tell light from dark, which helps them find their way.
So a starfish has eyes on its hands and can grow a spare body. Honestly, show off.
beats.text:
EYES ON ITS
HANDS.
SHOW OFF.

beats.say: True or false? A group of crows is called a murder.
beats.quiz:
A GROUP OF
CROWS IS CALLED
A MURDER
beats.bonus: Crows can recognize human faces and remember a person who bothered them for years.

beats.say: True. It sounds like a horror movie, but it's real.
The name comes from old English hunting books, hundreds of years ago, which had fun names for groups of animals. Most were forgotten. A murder of crows stuck.
Crows also use tools. Some crows bend twigs into hooks to fish bugs out of holes, and city crows have been seen dropping nuts on roads so cars crack them open.
And crows are brilliant. Researchers in Seattle wore a scary mask while catching a few crows. Years later, crows still scolded anyone wearing that mask, even crows that were never caught.
So be nice to crows. They remember faces, and they tell their friends.
beats.text:
THEY REMEMBER.
THEY TELL
THEIR FRIENDS.

beats.say: True or false? A platypus glows under ultraviolet light.
beats.quiz:
A PLATYPUS
GLOWS UNDER
UV LIGHT
beats.bonus: Male platypuses have venomous spurs on their back legs. They're one of the very few venomous mammals.

beats.say: True! Scientists found it in twenty twenty.
Under ultraviolet light, platypus fur glows a blueish green. Researchers noticed it while shining UV light on museum specimens.
Nobody knows for sure why. The platypus already lays eggs, has a duck bill, and the males have venom spurs on their legs. Glowing just got added to the list.
The platypus is what happens when nature uses every leftover part in the box.
beats.text:
EVERY LEFTOVER
PART IN
THE BOX

beats.say: True or false? The ostrich is the fastest animal on land.
beats.quiz:
THE OSTRICH IS
THE FASTEST
LAND ANIMAL
beats.bonus: An ostrich's eye is bigger than its brain.

beats.say: False. Fast, but not the fastest.
An ostrich can run around forty three miles an hour, which makes it the fastest bird on land. But a cheetah can hit around sixty five or seventy miles an hour in a short sprint.
Ostriches also don't bury their heads in the sand, by the way. They lower their heads to turn their eggs in a nest dug in the ground, and from far away it looks like the head disappeared.
Here's where the ostrich wins, though. A cheetah is done after a few hundred yards. An ostrich can keep up a fast pace for a long way. Sprinter versus marathon runner.
So the cheetah wins the race. The ostrich wins the race after the race.
True or false? A duck's quack doesn't echo.
beats.bonus: In mallards, it's usually the females that make the loud classic quack. The males sound quieter and raspier.

beats.say: False. This one went viral, and it's just wrong.
Acoustic scientists in England tested it, with a duck called Daisy, in a special echo room. Her quack echoed just fine.
The echo is just hard to notice. A quack fades out slowly, so the echo blends right into it. Your ears don't pick it apart.
So the duck's quack echoes. It's just a very sneaky echo.
True or false? Hummingbirds can fly backwards.
beats.bonus: A hummingbird's heart can beat over a thousand times a minute when it's busy.

beats.say: True. They're the only birds that can really do it.
Hummingbirds can twist their wings in a figure eight, so they push air on the way up and the way down. That lets them hover, fly sideways, and fly backwards.
To power all that, a hummingbird has to eat constantly, visiting hundreds of flowers a day. At night, some go into a deep sleep called torpor, where their body cools right down to save energy.
They beat their wings dozens of times every second. That's where the humming sound comes from.
A hummingbird is basically a tiny helicopter that drinks sugar water.
True or false? A mantis shrimp can punch hard enough to crack aquarium glass.
beats.quiz:
A SHRIMP CAN
PUNCH THROUGH
GLASS
beats.bonus: Mantis shrimp have many more types of color sensors in their eyes than humans do.

beats.say: True. Meet the strongest punch in the ocean.
A mantis shrimp's club shoots out so fast that the water around it boils into tiny bubbles. When those bubbles pop, they make a flash of light and a second shockwave.
They use it to smash open crabs and snail shells. And yes, people keeping them in small tanks have reported cracked glass.
A shrimp that punches so hard the water sparks. Do not shake its hand.
True or false? Elephants can't jump.
beats.bonus: Elephants can pick up rumbles through the ground with their feet, from other elephants far away.

beats.say: True. A grown elephant never has all four feet off the ground.
Their leg bones point almost straight down, and they're carrying several tons. Even when an elephant moves fast, at least one foot stays on the ground.

Baby elephants can't jump either, but they do something cute instead. For their first months, many calves don't really know what to do with their trunks, and they swing them around like a floppy rubber hose.
But they don't need to jump. Elephants can walk surprisingly fast, swim, and even feel low rumbles from other elephants through their feet.
The elephant can't jump, and honestly, the ground is grateful.

Scores! The fakes were the pink baby flamingos, the ostrich being fastest, and the duck with no echo. Everything else is real. Drop your score out of twelve in the comments, and tell me which one you still don't believe.
